props.name: adsorbed H2/CO independent of gas phase
props.statement: The composition of the adsorbed phase (H2(a)/CO(a)) did not depend on that of the gas phase in spite of an about eight-thousand-fold change of the partial pressure ratio, in synthesis with and without the liquid-nitrogen trap and in methanol decomposition.

props.name: rate equation agrees with Uchida-Ogino
props.note: Eq. 2 and its conditions are cited from Uchida and Ogino (ref. 5), not measured in this source
props.statement: Eq. 1 (n = 0.75) is in good agreement with the equation r = k(PH2²PCO)^(1−α), α = 0.3, previously reported by Uchida and Ogino, in spite of their different conditions (300-360 °C, 90-150 kg/cm2 vs 250 °C, 100-760 mmHg).

props.name: Langmuir-type adsorption inappropriate
props.note: the authors also cite Uchida and Ogino (ref. 12) that the rate cannot be expressed by any Langmuir-type equation; that is a cited result
props.statement: The rate equations could be read as a partially covered surface with Langmuir-type adsorption, but considerable amounts of adsorption are involved (Table I), so applying Langmuir-type adsorption seems inappropriate.

props.name: methanol far below equilibrium
props.statement: The amounts of methanol formed were far less than those calculated from the equilibrium constant and from the circulating rate.

props.name: H2 and CO adsorption mutually enhanced
props.statement: The amounts of hydrogen and carbon monoxide adsorbed during the reaction were greater than those adsorbed separately with the corresponding amounts introduced, indicating a marked mutual influence on the adsorption of each gas in the presence of the other; adsorption during the reaction cannot be estimated from results in the absence of the other gas.

props.name: products methanol and CO2
props.statement: The observed products were usually methanol and carbon dioxide and, depending on the conditions, small amounts of water and a trace of methane.

props.name: results reproducible with evacuation before each run
props.statement: With the catalyst evacuated for 3 hr at 400 °C before each run, the experimental results were satisfactorily reproducible.

props.name: water vapor kept from contaminating the catalyst
props.note: the source states the precaution only; it reports no measured effect of water vapor on the catalyst
props.statement: When the circulating rate was measured with a soap-film meter connected through stop-cocks I and J, precautions were taken to prevent water vapor from contaminating the catalyst.

props.name: Eley-Rideal hydrogenation of the surface complex is rate-determining
props.statement: The Eley-Rideal-type hydrogenation of the CH3O surface complex by gaseous hydrogen is the rate-determining step of methanol synthesis (the authors 'conclude' it may be so; the Summary says it 'has been suggested').

props.name: most adsorbed H2 and CO form a CH3O surface complex
props.statement: The constancy of the adsorbed-phase composition suggests that most of the adsorbed hydrogen and carbon monoxide (more than 80% of the hydrogen and 75% of the carbon monoxide) form a complex, and the average H2(a)/CO(a) value of 1.5 suggests its stoichiometric formula is CH3O.

props.name: closed circulating system with cylindrical reaction vessel A (Fig. 1)
props.description: Cylindrical reaction vessel (A) 85 mm long, 25 mm i.d.; the circulating gas is preheated through the central tube before the 45 mm catalyst bed; electric heater (B) regulated within ±2 °C; thermocouple (D); electromagnetically driven glass-piston circulation pump (K); methanol collected in a liquid-nitrogen trap (F); circulating-system volume about 433 ml at 250 °C; pressure and gas composition measured at intervals; gases and condensed products analysed by gas chromatography (silica gel and 13X molecular sieve columns, helium carrier; polyethylene glycol on Celite 545 and 5A molecular sieve at 60 °C, hydrogen carrier); circulating rate measured with a soap-film meter.
